title: The DC-DC workaround for LR2021 is flagging as a potential buffer overrun

labels.name: resolved
labels.description: Issue was resolved (e.g. bug fixed, or feature implemented)

body:
TLDR: The DC-DC workaround introduced in https://github.com/jgromes/RadioLib/pull/1864 triggers ASAN warnings, indicating a buffer overrun. **Describe the bug** `LR2021::setDCDCworkaround()` and `LR2021::resetDCDCworkaround()` pass `sizeof(uint32_t)` as the `len` argument of `readRegMem32()` / `writeRegMem32()`. Both functions count `len` in 32-bit words: `readRegMem32()` reads `len*sizeof(uint32_t)` bytes and fills `data[0..len-1]`, and `writeCommon()` sends `len` words. So each call moves 4 words where 1 is intended. In `src/modules/LR2021/LR2021_cmds_chip_control.cpp` (added in `67d7121d2a`, unchanged on master `bf07c6dd4`): - line 352: `readRegMem32(RADIOLIB_LR2021_REG_DCDC_ADC_CTRL, &adcCtrlRaw, sizeof(adcCtrlRaw))` writes `data[1..3]`, which is 12 bytes of stack past the local `uint32_t adcCtrlRaw`. - lines 374 and 390: `writeRegMem32(RADIOLIB_LR2021_REG_DCDC_FREQ_LF, &freq_lf, sizeof(freq_lf))` reads 12 bytes of stack past the local `uint32_t freq_lf`, and sends them to the three registers after `DCDC_FREQ_LF`. Both functions run from inside the driver: `setDCDCworkaround()` from `setRxPath()`, `resetDCDCworkaround()` from `setPacketType()`. So every LR2021 user reaches them during `begin()` and on `setRxBoostedGainMode()`, on either regulator. The first word is correct, so the workaround itself appears to work, which is why it passes on hardware. Semtech's reference implementation, which these functions port (`lr20xx_workarounds.c` in Lora-net/usp `351b2015`), passes `1` at each of these calls. Found with AddressSanitizer in a host build, using a stub HAL that answers every SPI byte with a CMD_OK status (0x04). cppcheck 2.17.1 with the repo's settings, and GCC 14 with `-Warray-bounds=2 -Wstringop-overflow=4`, don't flag it.
